scope: Proposition 3.2 (Neighborhood transfer) of the manuscript “Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold” (preprints/Graph-Decompositions-at-the-Integral-Expectation-Threshold-October-5-2026/graph-threshold-decompositions.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 175 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5c0b3a5fc1764ff3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute integer N1 such that the following holds for every n ≥ N1 and every r, s satisfying (3.3). There exists D = D(n, r, s) ⊆ 2E(Kn) with µr(D) ≥ 1 − 1/K0 such that, whenever • Y ⊆ [n] has |Y | ≤ n2/3; • J is a labelled bipartite graph with all edges between Y and [n] \ Y , and E(J) ⊆ E(G) for some G ∈ D; • at most n/8 vertices outside Y have positive degree in J, and all of those degrees are at most s; one has pc(J; n) ≤ r∗ := 1 − (1 − r)32 ≤ 32r. (3.4)
